gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans: Wide, stencil-flat, and sure of itself. Azonix holds every stroke to one thickness up top, while Noto Sans answers underneath with lowercase that fills most of the line height.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam reads full and open, its curve endings kept well apart and its s and z standing tall. Azonix, above it, is the sharper partner, spaghetti-like strokes of uniform width against a body with real variation.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unj: Flat, stenciled and commanding, Azonix leads. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined follows in modern sans-serif form, with generous gaps where curves meet stems and little difference between its cases, so paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-anatolian: Azonix draws every stroke at a single flat weight. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs sits beside it with outward-pointing tips and a lowercase rising near cap height, so the two feel like a loud voice and a modern, even-tempered one.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic reads clean and wide, with generous openings on its small letters and a pronounced x-height. Azonix gives it a heavy, commanding counterpart, so extended text would feel open and easy beneath a heading whose diagonals match its horizontals.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Azonix is all wide-mouthed authority, its curves and straights sharing one width. Noto Sans Armenian stays approachable below, and its body size can be generous, since the round letters open so invitingly.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Commanding from the first word, Azonix sets a single-weight, outlined tone up top. Noto Sans Avestan sits below with curve tips that never touch and a pronounced x-height, giving the heading's force somewhere clean to land.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Noto Sans Balinese reads modern and spacious, with breathing room inside every curve and ascenders kept short. Azonix is the one built to command attention in large letters, while Noto Sans Balinese does its best work quietly, carrying the sentences.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Authoritative from the first line, Azonix pours its letters out at one width. And Noto Sans Bamum is its opposite in temperament, its curved strokes ending before they turn inward and its counters wide open.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Azonix draws its round bowls in an outline that never swells or thins, and its capitals barely clear the lowercase. Noto Sans Bassa Vah handles the reading, its big midsection and open-jawed c carrying the text.
